decisions.rationale: In the title, 'breast-ovarian cancer' modifies the noun 'families' (20 breast-ovarian cancer families), so it functions as a disease mention used as a modifier rather than a standalone disease name.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate, Section 3: Annotate disease mentions that are used as Modifiers for other concepts

decisions.rationale: In the abstract, 'breast-ovarian cancer' again modifies 'families' ('20 breast-ovarian cancer families'), so it is annotated as a Modifier, consistent with the title mention.

decisions.rationale: 'breast and ovarian cancer' is a contiguous string referring to two separate diseases (breast cancer and ovarian cancer), and splitting it would lose information, so it is one Composite Mention.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate, Section 2: Annotate contiguous text strings (Composite Mention)

decisions.rationale: 'male breast cancer' denotes a distinct, specific form of breast cancer (occurring in men), so the gender token is included as it identifies a new form of the disease; it maps to one specific disease definition.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate, Section 2: Do not annotate gender (gender tokens included only if they identify a new form of the disease, e.g., 'male breast cancer')

decisions.rationale: 'breast-ovarian syndrome' names one specific hereditary syndrome linked to BRCA1 germ-line mutations rather than a family of multiple diseases; the qualifier 'breast-ovarian' makes it a specific named disease despite the general word 'syndrome'.
